## Cycle 5 outcome: PASSED (2026-07-30)
All 16 criteria verified. NEW BASELINES (both changed intentionally this cycle):
  ruff check . = 0 errors (was 286);  pytest tests/unit = 0 failed / 338 passed / 8 skipped
  on Windows (was 6 failed / 338 passed / 2 skipped). On Linux/CI the 6 POSIX permission
  tests RUN and pass -> 0 failed / 344 passed / 2 skipped.

MAJOR FIND — a real, user-facing product bug was discovered and fixed:
the `add_recipe_ingredients` MCP tool was NOT REGISTERED. Its `@mcp.tool()` decorator and
`def add_recipe_ingredients(request: str, clear_first: bool = False) -> dict:` header had
been dropped by a botched edit, leaving the entire function body as unreachable dead code
after `add_products_by_id`'s return — which is exactly what produced the F821 undefined-name
reports for `request` / `clear_first`. The tool is documented in README, CLAUDE.md,
.github/copilot-instructions.md, and mcp_server.py:9, but did not exist at runtime. The
Tester confirmed against `git show HEAD:mcp_server.py` that the lines were genuinely absent,
that the restored signature matches the orphaned docstring and the docs, that the body
references both params correctly, that the tool now registers, and that `add_products_by_id`
is undisturbed. ACCEPTED.

Other adjudications:
(a) `session_maintenance/updated_functions` added to ruff extend-exclude — 20 of the 22 F821
    sites live in a MACHINE-GENERATED self-healing fragment (header: "Auto-generated by
    nodriver self_healing on 2026-07-15") that scripts/apply_updates.py splices as TEXT into
    session_maintenance/flows.py, where every name resolves. Never imported as a module.
    Follows the debug_logs precedent. ACCEPTED — no hand-authored F821 hidden.
(b) The design predicted 6 rule classes summing to 286; ELEVEN appeared. Five were
    unanticipated: W291(4), E402(3), F541(2), E703(1), W292(1). Four auto-fixed; the 3 E402
    are `# noqa: E402` on imports that legitimately follow `sys.path.insert()` in
    scripts/seed_from_sources.py. ACCEPTED.
(c) F841/E722 deferred via [tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores] scoped ONLY to
    session_maintenance/** and utility/**; the 3 F841 in recipe_grabber.py (outside the
    scoped trees) were fixed individually. Global select/ignore untouched.

CI now: ci.yml lints `ruff check .` (all first-party) and runs the full `pytest tests/unit`,
both gating; a `typecheck` mypy job runs ADVISORY (continue-on-error: true); a new
.github/workflows/docker-build.yml runs the compose build scoped to main push/PR with a path
filter, setting a throwaway DATABASE_PASSWORD and creating an empty .env for interpolation.
Also fixed the Cycle 4 cosmetic leftover: auto_grocer_mcp/server.py line 1 docstring.

DEFERRED TECH DEBT (post-release): F841/E722 in session_maintenance/ + utility/; tightening
mypy from advisory to gating; test coverage for session_maintenance/ and utility/, which
remain essentially untested.

## Cycle 5 design (Product Designer, Mode C) — CI & quality gates

goal: >
  Turn the invisible lint debt into an enforced, red-gating quality bar for the first public
  release WITHOUT introducing unguarded regressions. Clear every mechanically-safe cosmetic
  lint class and every F821 (undefined-name, a POTENTIAL REAL NameError) across first-party
  code; defer the two judgment-call classes (F841, E722) in the untested legacy trees via a
  scoped, documented ignore rather than hand-editing behavior; make the unit suite green on
  Windows AND Linux without weakening the POSIX 0o600 security assertion; expand
  .github/workflows/ci.yml to lint ALL first-party code and run the FULL unit suite on every
  push/PR; add an advisory (non-blocking) type-check job and a scoped Docker-build check; and
  fix the Cycle-4 cosmetic docstring leftover.

non_goals:
  - CHANGELOG / v0.1.0 tag / GitHub Release (Cycle 6).
  - Re-opening Cycles 1-4 (secrets, licensing/attribution, docs, hygiene, the rename).
  - Any change to hyphenated on-disk runtime names (~/.texas-grocery-mcp/, the Docker volume,
    keyring SERVICE_NAME) — permanent per Cycle 4.
  - Linting/reformatting the vendored auto_grocer_mcp/ tree — it stays extend-excluded.
    (The single one-line docstring edit in Q-9 is a targeted content fix, not reformatting.)
  - Adding new RUNTIME dependencies. (mypy is dev-only tooling in requirements-dev.txt.)
  - Rewriting F841/E722 in the untested trees (deliberately deferred, see Q-4).
  - Making mypy or the Docker build red-gate the release (both stay non-blocking / scoped).

scope_and_approach: >
  ### SCOPING-QUESTION ANSWER (stated up front): OPTION (b).
  Fix F821 + the auto-fixable cosmetics (I001, W293, F401) now; defer the residual
  behavior-touching classes (F841, E722) in the untested trees via a scoped
  `per-file-ignores`; then red-gate CI on a now-clean tree.

  Justification against release risk:
    - (a) "fix all 286 then gate" forces hand-editing F841 (unused-local removal) and E722
      (`except:` -> `except Exception:`, which CHANGES what is caught) inside
      session_maintenance/ and utility/ — code with essentially NO test coverage (the 338
      passing tests are the vendored upstream suite, which is ruff-excluded and untouched by
      this work). Regression risk with no safety net, for near-zero release value.
    - (c) "advisory only, fix nothing" leaves F821 unfixed. F821 is undefined-name and can be
      a genuine runtime NameError. Shipping known potential bugs in a first public release is
      not "safe."
    - (b) fixes the one dangerous class (F821, each site reviewed individually) plus the
      classes ruff can fix deterministically (`--fix`), while deferring exactly the two
      judgment classes that alter behavior in unguarded code. Because the residuals are
      suppressed via a narrow scoped ignore, `ruff check .` reaches 0, so CI can red-gate
      IMMEDIATELY — it blocks nothing today and enforces cleanliness going forward. The
      deferral is tracked tech-debt for a post-release cycle.

  Q-1 — Triage (must run FIRST; produces the worklist).
    Capture `ruff check . --statistics` and `ruff check . --output-format=concise`. Extract:
      - `ruff check . --select F821 --output-format=concise` -> the MANUAL-REVIEW list.
      - `--select F841` and `--select E722` -> confirm these concentrate in
        session_maintenance/ and utility/. ANY F841/E722 landing OUTSIDE those two trees MUST
        be fixed individually in Q-4 (it lives in maintained/tested surface — mcp_server.py,
        tests/, classes/, database/, recipe_grabber.py — and must not be suppressed).
    Record baseline counts (expected total 286; the six classes should sum to 286 — flag any
    other rule that appears).

  Q-2 — Auto-fix the safe cosmetic classes.
    `ruff check . --select I001,W293,F401 --fix`. Then REVIEW THE DIFF OF EVERY first-party
    __init__.py — classes/__init__.py, database/__init__.py, session_maintenance/__init__.py —
    for F401 re-export side effects. Ruff honors __all__, so a symbol re-exported via __all__
    is left alone; but an __init__.py that re-exports WITHOUT __all__ will be mis-fixed. Where
    a removed import was a deliberate re-export, either add it to __all__ or annotate
    `# noqa: F401`. (auto_grocer_mcp/**/__init__.py is ruff-excluded and NOT touched.)
    Re-run `pytest tests/unit` after the auto-fix to confirm no import breakage.

  Q-3 — Manually review and fix EVERY F821.
    For each site: determine whether it is (i) a REAL BUG (missing import, typo,
    use-before-def) -> minimal fix; or (ii) a FALSE POSITIVE from dynamic/conditional
    definition -> resolve so ruff no longer flags it (add the import, restructure the guard,
    make the binding explicit). Do NOT blanket-suppress F821 with `# noqa` — surfacing real
    bugs is the whole point. Because session_maintenance/ and utility/ are untested, keep each
    fix minimal and behavior-preserving and DOCUMENT EACH F821 SITE + ITS RESOLUTION in the dev
    notes. End state: `ruff check . --select F821` returns 0.

  Q-4 — Defer residual F841 + E722 via SCOPED ignore (do NOT blanket-rewrite).
    F841 (unused local) can be an intentional debugging hold; E722 (bare `except:`) rewriting
    changes catch semantics (drops KeyboardInterrupt/SystemExit). Both need judgment, both
    concentrate in untested code.
    Add to pyproject.toml:
      [tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
      # Deferred to a post-release cleanup cycle: F841 (unused locals, some are
      # intentional debugging holds) and E722 (bare except) in the untested
      # session_maintenance/ + utility/ trees. Fixing them by hand pre-release is
      # unguarded (no test coverage). Tracked as tech debt.
      "session_maintenance/**" = ["F841", "E722"]
      "utility/**" = ["F841", "E722"]
    Do NOT add F841/E722 to the global [tool.ruff.lint] ignore — they stay enforced everywhere
    else. Any F841/E722 flagged outside the two scoped trees is FIXED INDIVIDUALLY here.
    After Q-2->Q-4, verify `ruff check .` returns 0.

  Q-5 — Fix the 6 Windows permission-test failures (platform-aware; POSIX assertion preserved).
    Exactly six tests fail with `assert 438 == 384` (0o666 vs 0o600 = SECURE_FILE_MODE,
    auto_grocer_mcp/utils/secure_file.py L15):
      - tests/unit/test_secure_file.py L18  test_creates_file_with_correct_permissions
      - tests/unit/test_secure_file.py L61  test_fixes_insecure_permissions_on_existing_file
      - tests/unit/test_secure_file.py L99  test_fixes_insecure_permissions
      - tests/unit/test_secure_file.py L111 test_leaves_secure_permissions_unchanged
      - tests/unit/test_secure_file.py L123 test_handles_world_readable_file
      - tests/unit/test_credentials.py  L88 test_encrypted_file_permissions
    Guard each with
      @pytest.mark.skipif(sys.platform == "win32",
                          reason="POSIX file-mode enforcement; Windows cannot set 0o600")
    (add `import sys` where missing). Use skipif on the WHOLE test (each test's purpose IS the
    permission check). DO NOT WEAKEN THE ASSERTION — keep `== 0o600` / `== SECURE_FILE_MODE`
    byte-for-byte. The guard must be `sys.platform == "win32"`-specific, NEVER an unconditional
    skip/xfail, so on Linux/macOS (the CI ubuntu runner and the Docker image) the assertion
    still runs and enforces the real security property.
    Expected: WINDOWS `pytest tests/unit` -> 0 failed / 338 passed / 8 skipped (the 6 move
    failed->skipped; 2 pre-existing + 6). LINUX/CI -> 0 failed / 344 passed / 2 skipped.

  Q-6 — Expand .github/workflows/ci.yml (gating lint + full test).
    - Lint step -> `ruff check .` (drop the narrow `mcp_server.py utility/graphql_cart.py
      tests/` scope; auto_grocer_mcp stays excluded via pyproject). Update the stale L34
      comment.
    - Test step -> `pytest tests/unit` (full suite; the 6 POSIX tests run and pass on ubuntu).
    - Keep triggers: push + pull_request to `dev` and `main`. Both jobs gating (no
      continue-on-error).
    - ORDERING DEPENDENCY: the lint step must only be flipped to `ruff check .` AFTER Q-2->Q-4
      make the tree clean (0). Flipping it first would red every PR.

  Q-7 — Docker build check (scoped, gating on the release path only).
    Add a SEPARATE workflow .github/workflows/docker-build.yml running
    `docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml build mcp`, triggered ONLY on push to `main`
    + pull_request targeting `main`, and PATH-FILTERED to Docker-relevant files (docker/**,
    requirements.txt, requirements-dev.txt, mcp_server.py, auto_grocer_mcp/**,
    pyproject.toml). Justification: the image installs Chromium/nodriver — heavy, slow, and
    network-flake-prone; running it on every dev-branch PR would drag the loop. A separate file
    is required because per-job trigger/path scoping is not possible within one workflow's `on:`.
    GOTCHA TO ENCODE: `docker compose ... build` interpolates the ENTIRE compose file first,
    and docker/docker-compose.yml uses `${DATABASE_PASSWORD:?...}` (mandatory-var), which
    ABORTS if unset. The job MUST set a throwaway `DATABASE_PASSWORD: ci` in its `env:` (no
    secret needed — the build never starts Postgres).

  Q-8 — Add type checking (ADVISORY / NON-BLOCKING — explicitly not a gate this cycle).
    - Add `mypy` to requirements-dev.txt (dev-only tooling; not a runtime dep).
    - Add [tool.mypy] to pyproject.toml: python_version = "3.12",
      ignore_missing_imports = true, and `exclude` covering auto_grocer_mcp, debug_logs,
      word_dictionaries, tests.
    - Add a `typecheck` CI job with `continue-on-error: true`, running mypy over the
      first-party source (excluding auto_grocer_mcp). It reports but does NOT block; it can be
      tightened / red-gated in a later cycle.

  Q-9 — Fix the Cycle-4 cosmetic docstring leftover.
    auto_grocer_mcp/server.py line 1 reads `"""Texas Grocery MCP Server - FastMCP entry
    point."""` -> `"""Auto Grocer MCP Server - FastMCP entry point."""`. This is the ONLY edit
    under auto_grocer_mcp/; it does not affect the ruff count (tree remains excluded).

risks_and_dependencies:
  - AUTO-FIX BREAKING __init__.py RE-EXPORTS (F401). ruff --fix removing a deliberately
    re-exported import consumed elsewhere -> ImportError. Mitigation: review every first-party
    __init__.py diff (Q-2), use __all__ / # noqa: F401; full suite as a net — BUT THE NET IS
    WEAK because the untested dirs are barely exercised (criterion 5).
  - F841/E722 BEHAVIOR CHANGES IN UNTESTED CODE — precisely why they are DEFERRED via scoped
    ignore (Q-4) rather than hand-edited. Residual risk: the deferral hides real defects
    (accepted, tracked tech-debt). Any F841/E722 outside the two dirs is fixed individually.
  - F821 FIXES ARE UNGUARDED in session_maintenance/ + utility/ — a wrong "fix" could alter
    behavior with no test to catch it. Mitigation: minimal, behavior-preserving edits, each
    documented. THIS IS THE SINGLE RISKIEST PART OF THIS CYCLE.
  - session_maintenance/ + utility/ HAVE ESSENTIALLY NO TEST COVERAGE. The 338 passing tests
    are mostly the vendored upstream suite, which is ruff-excluded and untouched — so the lint
    fixes land largely on code the suite does not exercise.
  - RED-GATING BEFORE THE TREE IS CLEAN BLOCKS ALL PRs. Hard ordering dependency: Q-6's
    `ruff check .` gating step must be flipped AFTER Q-2->Q-4 reach 0.
  - DOCKER BUILD JOB SLOW/FLAKY in CI (Chromium/nodriver install, network). Mitigation: scoped
    to main + Docker-relevant paths; can be downgraded to continue-on-error if flaky. Plus the
    ${DATABASE_PASSWORD:?...} interpolation gotcha — the build fails at PARSE time without a
    dummy value (criterion 15).
  - RUFF VERSION DRIFT. requirements-dev.txt pins `ruff>=0.6.0` (no upper bound); --fix
    behavior and rule membership vary by version, so "0 errors" locally may differ in CI.
    Mitigation: run the count checks with the same ruff the CI installs.
  - MYPY ADVISORY MISREAD AS A GATE. It will likely emit many errors on untested first-party
    code; continue-on-error: true keeps it non-blocking.
  - TEST-GUARD SECURITY REGRESSION. If the skipif were made unconditional (not win32-specific),
    the 0o600 property would stop being tested on POSIX — a SILENT SECURITY REGRESSION.
    Guarded by criteria 9 and 11.

### Q-3 — every F821 site + planned resolution (criterion 2 enumeration)
1. `mcp_server.py:703` `request` (also `clear_first` in same block): the body of the
   documented `add_recipe_ingredients` MCP tool is ORPHANED DEAD CODE — it sits after
   `add_products_by_id`'s `return _add_by_id_sync(...)`, its `@mcp.tool()` decorator + `def
   add_recipe_ingredients(request: str, clear_first: bool = False) -> dict:` header were
   dropped by a botched edit. No `def add_recipe_ingredients` exists anywhere in the repo, yet
   README/CLAUDE.md/copilot-instructions/mcp_server.py:9 all document it. **REAL LATENT BUG.**
   Resolution: restore the 2 dropped lines (decorator + def header) — the params are fully
   documented in the orphaned Args docstring and every sibling tool uses the identical pattern.
   ⚠️ BEHAVIOR-CHANGING (registers a tool that is currently unregistered) in code with no unit
   coverage → **FLAGGED FOR HUMAN REVIEW** per the design. Alternative considered: delete the
   dead block (runtime-identical but erases a documented flagship tool) — rejected as more
   destructive for a pre-release cycle.
2. `utility/beautiful_soup.py:23` `text`: `text = " ".join(text.split())` uses `text` before
   assignment because the `text = soup.get_text()` line directly above is commented out →
   guaranteed NameError in this scratch/demo script. Resolution: restore `text = soup.get_text()`.
3-22. `session_maintenance/updated_functions/change_store_via_ui.py` (20 sites: HEB_HOME,
   random_time×7, is_visible×2, click_element×2, _click_first_xpath×4, asyncio×2, xpath_all,
   human_like_typing, select_one): this is a GENERATED self-healing fragment ("Auto-generated
   by nodriver self_healing … Review before applying") that `scripts/apply_updates.py` splices
   as TEXT into `session_maintenance/flows.py`, where all these names resolve. It is never
   imported/executed as a module, so these are NOT real bugs — they are expected free names in
   a code fragment. Resolution: treat the generated-artifact directory like debug_logs and add
   `session_maintenance/updated_functions` to ruff `extend-exclude` (lint-time only, zero
   runtime effect, no source edited). ⚠️ FLAGGED: this deviates from "fix every F821 in first-
   party code" — justified because the dir is generated output, not hand-authored source, and
   suppressing F821 via `# noqa` (forbidden by the design) would be worse. End state:
   `ruff check . --select F821` → 0.

### Approach / ordering
Q-1 (done) → Q-2 auto-fix + review __init__ diffs + re-run suite → Q-3 → Q-4 → Q-5 →
verify `ruff check .`==0 and Windows pytest → THEN Q-6 (flip CI lint LAST) + Q-8 typecheck
job + Q-7 docker-build workflow + Q-9 docstring → full verification block.

### Risks / notes
- Re-export risk (criterion 5): the only first-party `__init__.py` with imports is
  `database/__init__.py`, and every import is in `__all__` (ruff honors it) → no F401 removal
  there. `classes/__init__.py` is whitespace-only; `session_maintenance/__init__.py` is a
  docstring. Risk is near-nil but the diff is still reviewed.
- Q-7 gotcha: `docker/docker-compose.yml` also has `env_file: ../.env` (gitignored, absent in

  empty repo-root `.env` before building, in addition to setting the throwaway
  `DATABASE_PASSWORD: ci` for the `${DATABASE_PASSWORD:?…}` interpolation.

## Cycle 4 design (Product Designer, Mode C) — Package rename texas_grocery_mcp -> auto_grocer_mcp

goal: >
  Rename the vendored Python package directory texas_grocery_mcp/ to auto_grocer_mcp/ and
  rewrite every PYTHON IDENTIFIER `texas_grocery_mcp` (underscores) to `auto_grocer_mcp`
  across the ~30 files that reference it — internal package imports, mcp_server.py, the
  entire tests/ tree (including the string `patch("texas_grocery_mcp....")` mock targets),
  two first-party consumer scripts, and the packaging/CI/agent config — so that shipping a
  ~93-95% verbatim hard fork of Michael Walker's MIT-licensed texas-grocery-mcp no longer
  imports under the upstream author's own project name (which can imply endorsement). Every
  MIT attribution obligation is preserved and made explicit AFTER the rename. Crucially the
  on-disk/runtime SERVICE and SESSION names `texas-grocery-mcp` (HYPHENS) — the OS keyring
  SERVICE_NAME, the ~/.texas-grocery-mcp/ session directory, and the Docker volume mount
  paths — are left byte-for-byte unchanged, because changing them would orphan existing
  keyring entries, sessions, and volumes. The unit suite (6 failed / 338 passed / 2 skipped)
  is the safety net proving the import graph and the mock targets still resolve.

non_goals:
  - Changing any HYPHENATED on-disk/runtime name: keyring `SERVICE_NAME = "texas-grocery-mcp"`
    (auth/credentials.py L23), the ~/.texas-grocery-mcp/ path (config.py, clients/graphql.py
    docstrings, .gitignore, .dockerignore), or the Docker volume/mount
    /root/.texas-grocery-mcp (docker/docker-compose.yml, docker/Dockerfile.mcp).
  - Editing the two .github/skills/*/SKILL.md files that reference those hyphenated paths.
  - Ruff's 286 pre-existing errors, the 6 Windows-only pytest failures, CI expansion,
    Docker build-check (Cycle 5). Baselines must hold EXACTLY.
  - CHANGELOG / v0.1.0 tag / GitHub Release (Cycle 6).
  - Re-opening Cycles 1-3. The LICENSE TEXT and NOTICE/README attribution CONTENT from
    Cycle 1 are preserved; only package-path references and one clarifying clause change.
  - Rewriting the upstream project's NAME in attribution: the hyphenated string
    `texas-grocery-mcp` that names Michael Walker's project (and its GitHub URL) must STAY —
    that IS the attribution.
  - Editing this handoff file (it legitimately contains both old and new names).

scope_and_approach: >
  ### THE DISCRIMINATOR RULE (read first; applies to every work item)
  Two distinct tokens differ only by separator:
    - `texas_grocery_mcp` (UNDERSCORES) = Python package / import path / package dir name
      -> RENAME to `auto_grocer_mcp`. NO EXCEPTIONS.
    - `texas-grocery-mcp` (HYPHENS) = keyring service name, ~/.texas-grocery-mcp/ path,
      Docker volume/mount, OR the upstream project name/URL used for attribution
      -> KEEP UNCHANGED, except the small enumerated cosmetic/identity set in R-4 and R-5.

  Operational rule: replace the UNDERSCORE token globally; NEVER run a separator-insensitive
  (`texas.grocery.mcp`) or case-folded find/replace. Do the underscore pass first and verify
  it in isolation, then touch only the explicitly-listed hyphenated strings in R-4/R-5.
  A single file may legitimately contain BOTH tokens — e.g. tests/unit/test_credentials.py
  has `patch("texas_grocery_mcp.auth.credentials.KEYRING_AVAILABLE", ...)` (RENAME), the
  keyring args `"texas-grocery-mcp"` at L68/L71 (KEEP), and `tmp_path / ".texas-grocery-mcp"`
  at L18/L298 (KEEP). This CANNOT be a blanket per-file substitution.

  R-1 — Move the directory with history (FIRST, as a single Git rename).
    `git mv texas_grocery_mcp auto_grocer_mcp`. This moves the entire subtree — including
    texas_grocery_mcp/LICENSE -> auto_grocer_mcp/LICENSE — in one operation, so the upstream
    MIT LICENSE rides along BYTE-FOR-BYTE and Git records a rename (preserving git blame
    provenance). Do NOT delete-and-recreate. BEFORE the move, capture sha256 of
    texas_grocery_mcp/LICENSE; after, confirm it matches auto_grocer_mcp/LICENSE (criterion 5).
    The tree is broken until R-2/R-3 complete; that is expected.

  R-2 — Rewrite the Python identifier in all .py files:
    - Vendored package internals (~28 modules, now under auto_grocer_mcp/): all top-level
      and function-local imports — clients/graphql.py, clients/__init__.py, models/__init__.py,
      reliability/__init__.py, services/__init__.py, observability/{__init__,health,logging}.py,
      auth/{__init__,session,credentials,browser_refresh}.py,
      tools/{__init__,cart,coupon,product,session,store,substitution}.py, utils/__init__.py,
      state.py, server.py. (~72 internal import sites.)
    - mcp_server.py — the 11 function-local import sites plus the docstring reference (~13).
    - ENTIRE tests/ tree (~150 sites) — tests/conftest.py;
      tests/integration/{test_product_details_live,test_substitution_live}.py; all tests/unit/*.
      EXPLICITLY include the string `patch("texas_grocery_mcp....")` mock targets and dotted
      string args to mock.patch.object/patch(...) — these are STRING LITERALS, not imports, so
      an import-only sweep MISSES them. Confirmed concrete examples:
        tests/unit/test_cache.py L37 patch("texas_grocery_mcp.reliability.cache.datetime");
        test_cart_tools.py / test_cart_verification.py patch("texas_grocery_mcp.tools.cart....");
        test_coupon_tools.py patch("texas_grocery_mcp.tools.coupon....");
        test_credentials.py patch("texas_grocery_mcp.auth.credentials....");
        test_geocoding.py patch("texas_grocery_mcp.services.geocoding....");
        test_graphql_client.py "texas_grocery_mcp.clients.graphql.is_authenticated";
        test_health.py "texas_grocery_mcp.utils.config.get_settings";
        test_product_search_diagnostics.py "texas_grocery_mcp.clients.graphql....".
      Also the prose in tests/unit/test_graphql_cart.py L5.
    - First-party consumers: session_maintenance/auth_export.py (~L109),
      manual_scripts/test_graphql_mode.py (~L111).

  R-3 — Rewrite the underscore identifier in non-.py packaging / CI / agent config:
    - pyproject.toml L40 `extend-exclude = ["texas_grocery_mcp", ...]` -> "auto_grocer_mcp"
      (THIS is what keeps the vendored tree out of the ruff count — see risks), plus the
      provenance comment prose at L5/L8 and the exclude comment at L38.
    - requirements.txt L19 comment.
    - .github/workflows/ci.yml L34 comment.
    - .github/agents/developer.agent.md L38.
    - .github/agents/handoffs/oos-substitution.md package-path refs
      (L92/L93/L141/L142/L224/L225/L228/L244).
    - Package-path (slash) references in NOTICE and README.md -> auto_grocer_mcp/... (R-6).

  R-4 — Fix the dormant upstream identity. RECOMMENDATION: RENAME the identity string;
    do NOT delete the file.
    auto_grocer_mcp/server.py ~L162 hard-codes `FastMCP(name="texas-grocery-mcp", ...)` with
    instructions headed "## Texas Grocery MCP". This server is NEVER started — the real entry
    point is mcp_server.py L519 `FastMCP(name="auto-grocer")`, and a repo-wide search for
    `texas_grocery_mcp.server` finds NO importers (verified dormant). Change the identity to
    `name="auto-grocer-mcp"` and the heading to "## Auto Grocer MCP" (kept intentionally
    distinct from the canonical `auto-grocer` so it doesn't masquerade as the shipped server).
    Justification for rename over delete: (a) this is a rename cycle, not a deletion cycle —
    Cycle 3 already handled dead-code removal; (b) NOTICE cites .../server.py as a genuine fork
    modification (the find_substitute tool-registration line), so deleting would make that
    attribution claim stale and pull NOTICE editing into scope; (c) rename is trivially
    reversible. This hyphenated string is an ENUMERATED EXCEPTION to the discriminator rule.

  R-5 — Cosmetic user-visible install strings (the other enumerated hyphen exceptions).
    Replace `pip install texas-grocery-mcp[browser]` -> `pip install auto-grocer-mcp[browser]`
    at auth/browser_refresh.py L7, L302, L804, and tools/session.py L249. These are user-facing
    guidance strings, not a keyring/path/volume key and not attribution.

  R-6 — Update attribution wording so the derivation stays explicit AFTER the rename.
    In NOTICE, README.md Credits (~L273-279), and the pyproject.toml provenance comment (L5-8):
    KEEP every existing attribution element — "Michael Walker", the upstream URL
    https://github.com/mgwalkerjr95/texas-grocery-mcp (HYPHENS, KEEP), "MIT", "modified from
    the original" — repoint package-path references from texas_grocery_mcp/... to
    auto_grocer_mcp/... (including auto_grocer_mcp/LICENSE), and ADD a clause stating the
    package was FORMERLY IMPORTED AS `texas_grocery_mcp` so the lineage is traceable. The
    upstream MIT LICENSE TEXT must remain byte-for-byte verbatim — only surrounding prose changes.

  R-7 — KEEP list (verify untouched at the end).
    SERVICE_NAME = "texas-grocery-mcp" (credentials.py L23); ~/.texas-grocery-mcp/... in
    auth/credentials.py L59, utils/config.py L32, clients/graphql.py L84/L92/L921;
    .texas-grocery-mcp/ in .gitignore L48 and .dockerignore L34; /root/.texas-grocery-mcp in
    docker/docker-compose.yml L88 and docker/Dockerfile.mcp L46; the keyring-arg
    "texas-grocery-mcp" and .texas-grocery-mcp dir in tests/unit/test_credentials.py; and the
    upstream project name/URL in NOTICE/README/pyproject.

acceptance_criteria:
  1. Directory texas_grocery_mcp/ does NOT exist; auto_grocer_mcp/ exists and contains
     auth/credentials.py, clients/graphql.py, server.py, and LICENSE.
  2. `git grep -nE "texas_grocery_mcp"` (UNDERSCORES) across the whole repo EXCLUDING
     .github/agents/handoffs/public-release-prep.md returns ZERO matches.
  3. OVER-EAGER-REPLACEMENT GUARD: `git grep -nE "texas-grocery-mcp"` (HYPHENS) still returns
     matches, and each surviving match is in the KEEP set (R-7) — no hyphenated
     runtime/attribution name was rewritten except the enumerated R-4/R-5 strings.
  4. auto_grocer_mcp/auth/credentials.py still contains, byte-identical,
     `SERVICE_NAME = "texas-grocery-mcp"` (hyphens).
  5. LICENSE BYTE-IDENTICAL: sha256(auto_grocer_mcp/LICENSE) equals the sha256 of
     texas_grocery_mcp/LICENSE captured immediately before R-1, and it still contains
     `MIT` and `Michael Walker`.
  6. Runtime paths unchanged: docker/docker-compose.yml still mounts
     `...:/root/.texas-grocery-mcp`, docker/Dockerfile.mcp still runs
     `mkdir -p /root/.texas-grocery-mcp`, .gitignore/.dockerignore still ignore
     `.texas-grocery-mcp/`; utils/config.py and clients/graphql.py still reference
     `~/.texas-grocery-mcp/...`.
  7. pyproject.toml extend-exclude now lists "auto_grocer_mcp" and no longer lists
     "texas_grocery_mcp".
  8. Dormant-server identity fixed: auto_grocer_mcp/server.py FastMCP(name=...) is no longer
     "texas-grocery-mcp" and its instructions heading is no longer "## Texas Grocery MCP";
     mcp_server.py still contains `FastMCP(name="auto-grocer")` UNCHANGED.
  9. Cosmetic install strings updated: no `pip install texas-grocery-mcp[browser]` remains in
     auth/browser_refresh.py or tools/session.py.
  10. ATTRIBUTION EXPLICIT POST-RENAME: NOTICE, README.md Credits, and the pyproject.toml
      provenance comment each still contain "Michael Walker",
      github.com/mgwalkerjr95/texas-grocery-mcp, "MIT", and "modified from the original",
      AND each now states the package was formerly imported as `texas_grocery_mcp`.
  11. auto_grocer_mcp/LICENSE exists, and NOTICE/README.md/pyproject.toml reference
      auto_grocer_mcp/LICENSE (not texas_grocery_mcp/LICENSE).
  12. Every .py under auto_grocer_mcp/ parses: `python -m compileall -q auto_grocer_mcp`
      exits 0.
  13. `git grep -c "auto_grocer_mcp" mcp_server.py` >= 11 and
      `git grep -c "texas_grocery_mcp" mcp_server.py` == 0.
  14. FULL UNIT SUITE MATCHES BASELINE EXACTLY: `pytest tests/unit` = 6 failed / 338 passed /
      2 skipped, same categories/counts. This is the real proof the renamed imports and every
      patch("...") mock target resolve.
  15. LINT BASELINE HOLDS: `ruff check .` still reports 286 errors, confirming R-3 kept the
      vendored tree excluded under its new name.
  16. NO COEXISTENCE / LEFTOVER: `git ls-files texas_grocery_mcp` is empty and no
      texas_grocery_mcp/ path remains staged or on disk.

risks_and_dependencies:
  - BLIND FIND/REPLACE DESTROYING THE HYPHENATED RUNTIME NAMES. A separator-insensitive or
    over-broad substitution would rewrite SERVICE_NAME, the ~/.texas-grocery-mcp/ session dir,
    or the Docker volume mount — orphaning the user's OS-keyring credential entry, existing
    session files, and the mounted volume. Mitigation: the discriminator rule, enforced by
    criteria 3/4/6.
  - MISSED patch("texas_grocery_mcp....") STRING TARGETS. These are string literals, not
    imports, so an import-only sweep skips them. Once the old package dir is gone, a stale
    target raises ModuleNotFoundError at patch time — a LOUD failure caught by criterion 14.
    THE GENUINELY DANGEROUS EDGE is a PARTIAL MOVE WHERE OLD AND NEW PACKAGE DIRS COEXIST:
    a leftover texas_grocery_mcp/ lets a stale patch("texas_grocery_mcp...") resolve against
    the WRONG module object, so it SILENTLY FAILS TO INTERCEPT the code-under-test (which now
    imports auto_grocer_mcp) while the test may still pass — "patching nothing." Mitigation:
    single clean `git mv` with zero leftover (criterion 16), zero-underscore grep (2), and the
    full suite green at baseline (14).
  - `git mv` VS DELETE+ADD — LOSING HISTORY. Recreating the directory discards Git's rename
    tracking, breaking git blame provenance on the vendored MIT code and on the LICENSE —
    undesirable for an attribution-sensitive fork. Mitigation: R-1 mandates a single git mv;
    criterion 5 hashes the LICENSE to prove content survived.
  - THE MIT NOTICE SURVIVING THE MOVE. The LICENSE text moves for free inside R-1, but the
    surrounding attribution prose must be repointed to auto_grocer_mcp/LICENSE while KEEPING
    upstream's hyphenated project name and URL. An over-eager pass could FALSIFY the
    attribution by renaming the upstream project itself. Mitigation: R-6 + R-7, verified by
    criteria 10/11 and the hyphen-KEEP guard 3.
  - server.py RENAME VS DELETE. Chosen: rename (R-4). Deleting the dormant file would strand
    the NOTICE reference to .../server.py and widen scope.
  - RUFF EXCLUSION COUPLING (BASELINE DEPENDENCY). The 286-error baseline depends on
    pyproject.toml extend-exclude skipping the vendored tree. If the dir is renamed (R-1) but
    extend-exclude is not updated (R-3), ruff would suddenly lint ~33 vendored modules and the
    count would balloon. Mitigation: R-3; criterion 15 catches any miss.
  - CI DEPENDENCY. .github/workflows/ci.yml lints only mcp_server.py utility/graphql_cart.py
    tests/; the renamed test imports must parse (criteria 12/14). The L34 comment is cosmetic.

Removing them would violate C10. Keeping them satisfies C10 and creates a minor C2 tension,

invocation.** C2 and C10 are both satisfied; the 3 lineage occurrences are a documented

## Cycle 3 design (Product Designer, Mode C) — Repo hygiene

goal: >
  Remove dead weight and internal contradictions so a stranger cloning auto_grocer sees
  exactly one coherent story. Collapse the three competing dependency systems down to
  `requirements.txt` (runtime, single source of truth — already declared as such by
  pyproject.toml's `dynamic = ["dependencies"]`) plus `requirements-dev.txt` (dev),
  dropping Pipfile/Pipfile.lock and the stale unused `openai` pin; delete the dead
  `grocery_browser/` package and repoint every path reference to the real
  `session_maintenance/` package (including the already-broken `scripts/apply_updates.py`,
  which today reads from the wrong directory); de-duplicate the two identical
  DATABASE_IMPLEMENTATION.md files (keep docs/); delete the stale docs/README.md
  Best-README-Template boilerplate and the .github/push.yaml stub; and eliminate the weak
  hardcoded Postgres fallback password `grocer_user_123` in docker/docker-compose.yml in
  favor of a fail-fast required variable, while documenting the existing-volume migration
  risk. CLAUDE.md stays at the repo root unchanged (beyond one dead-path fix). No runtime
  behavior, no package rename, no lint cleanup.

non_goals:
  - The texas_grocery_mcp -> auto_grocer_mcp package rename (Cycle 4).
  - Ruff's 286 pre-existing errors, the 6 Windows-only 0o600 pytest failures, CI/type-check
    expansion, Docker build-check in CI (Cycle 5). No lint fixes designed here.
  - CHANGELOG / v0.1.0 tag / GitHub Release (Cycle 6).
  - Re-opening Cycle 1 (LICENSE/NOTICE/disclaimer/credits) or Cycle 2 (module names,
    broken links, cross-platform quickstart).
  - Deleting .github/agents/, .claude/, or .github/skills/ (owner decision 3 — kept as
    contributor tooling). In particular, do NOT edit the two SKILL.md files that correctly
    say grocery_browser.run "no longer exists" (Cycle 2 accepted exception).
  - Any change to on-disk runtime names: ~/.texas-grocery-mcp/, the auto_grocer_session /
    auto_grocer_pgdata Docker volume names, keyring SERVICE_NAME.
  - Relocating manual_scripts/ (nice-to-have, not release-blocking).

scope_and_approach: >
  Ordered work items. Each names real files and its required pre-deletion / pre-change
  verification (all offline). NOTE: the designer verified every claim below against the
  actual tree.

  H-1 — Consolidate the three dependency systems.
    Pre-change verification:

     still contains `dynamic = ["dependencies"]` with
     `dependencies = { file = ["requirements.txt"] }`.

     same for session_maintenance/self_healing.py both exit 0, and

      POSTGRES_PASSWORD and the DATABASE_URL values

      unavailable, criteria 10 & 11 fully cover the literal removal and fail-fast form.)

risks_and_dependencies:
  - Docker build depends on requirements.txt. Dockerfile.mcp L27-28 COPY + pip install, and
    ci.yml installs -r requirements.txt -r requirements-dev.txt (both verified). H-1 must
    KEEP requirements.txt/requirements-dev.txt and remove only Pipfile/Pipfile.lock + the
    openai line. Neither build nor CI uses pipenv, so removing the Pipfiles is inert.
  - Postgres password change can strand the existing auto_grocer_pgdata volume. Postgres
    bakes POSTGRES_PASSWORD at first init. Today ${DATABASE_PASSWORD} is usually empty at
    compose-interpolation time, so existing local volumes were initialized with the old
    literal grocer_user_123. After H-6, if the owner supplies a NEW DATABASE_PASSWORD the
    app's DATABASE_URL uses it but the existing volume still authenticates with the old one
    -> connection failure. Mitigation (documented in the compose comment): set
    DATABASE_PASSWORD=grocer_user_123 to keep the existing volume, OR
    `docker compose ... down -v` to recreate it (destroys local recipe/ingredient data —
    re-seed afterward). Pre-first-public-release, so only the owner holds a volume.
  - Removing openai could break an unnoticed import. Guarded by the pre-change grep
    (verified empty). claude.py uses anthropic.
  - Editing scripts/apply_updates.py and session_maintenance/self_healing.py: changes are
    path/string/docstring only — no logic or imports. Verified via ast.parse (criterion 6)
    and criterion 14. No test references grocery_browser or openai, so the deletions are
    inert to the pytest suite.
  - Baselines must not regress: ruff = 286, pytest = 6 failed / 338 passed / 2 skipped.
  - Scope guards: criterion 1 explicitly excludes .github/skills/ so the Cycle 2 accepted
    exception is preserved, and .github/agents/ / .claude/ are untouched.

## Cycle 2 design (Product Designer, Mode C)

goal: >
  Make auto_grocer's user-facing documentation literally true for a stranger who
  clones the repo. Fix every stale module reference (docs invoke the non-existent
  `grocery_browser.run`; the real module is `session_maintenance.run`, per main.py L22),
  repair the two broken README links (`docs/CLAUDE_SETUP.md`, `grocery_browser/README.md`),
  replace the Linux-only `source venv/bin/activate` Quick Start with a cross-platform
  create-your-own-venv flow (the repo `venv/` is a broken WSL venv; a fresh clone has
  none), document every prerequisite needed to reach a running MCP server, and lead with
  the recommended source-only Docker path. Scope is documentation correctness ONLY — no
  code behavior, no file renames, no dead-directory removal, no dependency consolidation,
  no re-opening of Cycle 1's WAF/legal work. After Cycle 2, every command and link a new
  user is told to run must resolve to something that actually exists.

non_goals:
  - Dependency-system consolidation (Pipfile vs requirements.txt vs pyproject.toml),
    the duplicate DATABASE_IMPLEMENTATION.md, removal of the dead grocery_browser/
    directory, and the docker-compose fallback password (all Cycle 3). Do NOT delete
    grocery_browser/ or edit .gitignore's grocery_browser/updated_functions/ rules.
  - The texas_grocery_mcp -> auto_grocer_mcp package rename (Cycle 4). Docs keep the
    current name.
  - Ruff's 286 pre-existing errors, the 6 Windows pytest permission failures, CI
    expansion (Cycle 5).
  - CHANGELOG / v0.1.0 tag / GitHub Release (Cycle 6).
  - ANY change to on-disk runtime names (~/.texas-grocery-mcp/, the auto_grocer_session
    Docker volume, keyring SERVICE_NAME) — permanently out of scope.
  - Re-opening Cycle 1 (LICENSE/NOTICE/disclaimer/credits, WAF-tone softening). Leave the
    "anti-bot evasion" wording in session_maintenance/README.md L15 alone — it is Cycle 1's
    domain and was intentionally left as accurate maintenance prose.

scope_and_approach: >
  All work is text edits to docs/prose (plus command strings inside two code-file
  docstrings). No importable code, no logic, no runtime behavior changes.

  D-1. Stale module references — replace every `python -m grocery_browser.run` with
       `python -m session_maintenance.run`, and every `python -m grocery_browser.waf_probe`
       with `python -m session_maintenance.waf_probe`. The `session_maintenance/` package
       is real (session_maintenance/run.py, session_maintenance/waf_probe.py exist);
       `grocery_browser/` has no run.py/waf_probe.py so those invocations error out today.
       Sites (verified by `git grep`):
         - README.md L53, L55, L69, L74 (command blocks / inline commands)
         - main.py L14, L15 (module docstring only — DO NOT touch imports/logic; main.py
           L22 already correctly imports session_maintenance.run)
         - main.py L6 docstring "delegates to ``grocery_browser.run``" and L4 "``grocery_browser`` package"
         - docs/ARCHITECTURE.md L7 ("`python -m grocery_browser.run`") and the package-name
           prose at L4/L8
         - session_maintenance/README.md L42, L47, L50, L55, L56, L57 (grocery_browser.run)
           and L60 (grocery_browser.waf_probe); the H1 title L1 "# grocery_browser — ..."
         - session_maintenance/run.py L22, L23 (module docstring usage examples only)
         - session_maintenance/waf_probe.py L12, L17 (module docstring only)
       The `.github/skills/refresh-heb-login/SKILL.md` L40 and
       `.github/skills/refresh-graphql-hashes/SKILL.md` L40 already state the module no
       longer exists — they are CORRECT; DO NOT edit the skills.

  D-2. Broken README links — repoint (do not create new stubs; equivalent docs exist):
         - README.md L170 `[Browser automation (nodriver)](grocery_browser/README.md)`
           -> `session_maintenance/README.md` (the actual browser-layer doc).
         - README.md L172 `[Claude Setup Guide](docs/CLAUDE_SETUP.md)` -> `CLAUDE.md`
           (CLAUDE.md contains the Claude/Anthropic API setup guide).
         - README.md L210 prose "See `docs/CLAUDE_SETUP.md` and `docs/POSTGRES_INSTALL.md`"
           -> replace CLAUDE_SETUP.md with CLAUDE.md; keep docs/POSTGRES_INSTALL.md (exists).
         - docs/ARCHITECTURE.md L20 `[grocery_browser/README.md](../grocery_browser/README.md)`
           -> `../session_maintenance/README.md`.
       Rationale for repoint over create: creating docs/CLAUDE_SETUP.md and
       grocery_browser/README.md would duplicate CLAUDE.md and session_maintenance/README.md
       (duplicate-doc cleanup is Cycle 3); the true content already lives elsewhere.

  D-3. Cross-platform Quick Start — in README.md replace the L14-16 block
       (`source venv/bin/activate`) with a CREATE-your-own-venv step giving BOTH:

## Owner decisions (CONFIRMED by the user — do not relitigate)
1. **License:** MIT for auto_grocer itself.
2. **Distribution:** source-only (git clone + `docker compose`). No PyPI, no GHCR.
3. **Agent scaffolding:** KEEP `.github/agents/` and `.claude/` public as contributor tooling.
4. **Git history:** use `git filter-repo` to scrub if secrets/PII are found in history
   (NOT a fresh repo). **The actual history rewrite is a destructive, hard-to-reverse
   operation — the developer MUST stop and get explicit user approval immediately before
   running it, and MUST create a backup clone/bundle first.**
5. **Vendored fork:** KEEP vendored, but RENAME the Python package
   `texas_grocery_mcp` → `auto_grocer_mcp`. Do NOT change the on-disk runtime names
   (`~/.texas-grocery-mcp/` session dir, the Docker volume, keyring `SERVICE_NAME`) —
   changing those orphans existing sessions and keyring entries. That is a deferred
   follow-up, explicitly out of scope.

---

## Release cycles (multi-cycle plan; ONE cycle per design→dev→test loop)
- **Cycle 1 — Secret & PII scrub + Legal/Licensing/Attribution.** (BLOCKERS. In progress.)
- **Cycle 2 — Docs correctness.** Stale module names, broken links, cross-platform quickstart.
- **Cycle 3 — Repo hygiene.** Dependency systems, duplicate docs, dead packages, compose password.
- **Cycle 4 — Package rename** `texas_grocery_mcp` → `auto_grocer_mcp`.
- **Cycle 5 — CI & quality gates.** Ruff coverage, type checking, Docker build check.
- **Cycle 6 — CHANGELOG, v0.1.0 tag, GitHub Release.**

## Architect audit findings (grounded; cite these — do not re-derive)

### Blockers
- **A1 — Real PII in `debug_logs/`.** Owner's email `benbond96@gmail.com`, full name,
  HEB user id `7463103707`, order ids `HEB188002693203319808` / `HEB197442000236280832`,
  store ids 243 / 14, cart totals `$118.21` / `$222.32`.
  Files: `debug_logs/session_20260609_102144/20260609_102419_265495_interrupted_test.html`,
  `debug_logs/session_20260715_134229/20260715_134718_440347_change_store_via_ui_Exception.html`,
  `debug_logs/waf_probe_20260707_214811.json`, `debug_logs/waf_probe_20260707_215004.json`
  (reese84 / Imperva token state + session cookie names).
- **A2 — Live `.env`** at repo root with HEB password, Gmail IMAP app password,
  `CLAUDE_API_KEY` (`sk-ant-…`), DB password. Gitignored (`.gitignore` L1) but history unverified.
- **A3 — MIT attribution gap.** `texas_grocery_mcp/` is a substantial portion of an MIT work
  (upstream: https://github.com/mgwalkerjr95/texas-grocery-mcp, MIT © Michael Walker) but ships
  with NO LICENSE file and NO per-file notice. Upstream's LICENSE was never copied.
- **A4 — No root LICENSE** → "all rights reserved" by default.
- **A5 — No disclaimer.** No "not affiliated with H-E-B", no trademark note, no
  personal-use limitation. README (~L106) reads as a WAF-evasion guide.

### Fork divergence (measured against real upstream v0.1.2)
- Vendored tree: ~33 modules, ≈8,000–8,500 LOC. **≈93–95% verbatim upstream**, flattened
  out of upstream's `src/` layout.
- Net-new: `texas_grocery_mcp/tools/substitution.py` (~340 LOC; the ONLY module importing
  first-party code — `from claude import evaluate_substitutes`, L274).
- Modified: ~40 LOC persisted-query override loader in `texas_grocery_mcp/clients/graphql.py`
  (~1,410 LOC total; docstring ref at L77); one tool-registration line in `server.py`.
- Deleted vs upstream: `src/` wrapper, `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`, Dockerfile, CHANGELOG,
  CONTRIBUTING, SECURITY, **and the LICENSE**.
- The project's heavy alterations live OUTSIDE the package, in `mcp_server.py` (~1,250 LOC),
  which consumes the fork as a library.
- Permanent hard fork: no submodule, no pinned SHA, no sync script, no upstream-tracking ADR.

### Coupling
- Vendored → first-party: exactly 1 import (substitution.py L274).
- First-party → vendored: 4 symbols only — `clients.graphql.HEBGraphQLClient`,
  `clients.graphql.reload_persisted_query_overrides`, `auth.session.is_authenticated`,
  `utils.config.get_settings`. Sites: `mcp_server.py` (11 function-local imports),
  `session_maintenance/auth_export.py` L109, `manual_scripts/test_graphql_mode.py` L111.
- Rename blast radius: **≈240+ occurrences across ~30 files** — 72 internal package imports,
  ~150 in `tests/unit/*` (including string `patch("texas_grocery_mcp....")` targets — these
  are easy to miss), ~13 in `mcp_server.py`, plus `pyproject.toml` ruff `extend-exclude`,
  `requirements.txt` comment, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`,
  `.github/agents/developer.agent.md`, `.github/agents/handoffs/oos-substitution.md`.

### Trademark/confusion
- The shipped product speaks as `auto-grocer` (`mcp_server.py` L519 `FastMCP(name="auto-grocer")`).
- But `texas_grocery_mcp/server.py` L161 hard-codes `FastMCP(name="texas-grocery-mcp")` in a
  runnable-but-dormant entry point; `texas_grocery_mcp/auth/credentials.py` L23 sets
  `SERVICE_NAME = "texas-grocery-mcp"` (becomes the OS keyring label).

### Required polish (later cycles)
- `grocery_browser.run` referenced throughout docs but does not exist — real module is
  `session_maintenance.run` (`main.py` L22). Sites: README L53/L69/L74/L177/L188,
  `main.py` L6, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` L8, `session_maintenance/README.md` L42.
  `.github/skills/refresh-heb-login/SKILL.md` L40 already says it no longer exists.
- Broken README links: `docs/CLAUDE_SETUP.md` (L172, L210), `grocery_browser/README.md` (L177).
- `docker/docker-compose.yml` L30 hardcodes fallback password `grocer_user_123`.
- Three dependency systems: `Pipfile`/`Pipfile.lock` vs `requirements.txt` vs `pyproject.toml`
  (which declares requirements.txt the single source of truth at L8). Stale
  `openai==0.28.0` in `requirements.txt` L11 despite the migration to `anthropic`.
- Duplicate `DATABASE_IMPLEMENTATION.md` at root and in `docs/`.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` L34 lints only 3 paths; no type checking.
- `.github/push.yaml` is a one-line stub, not a valid workflow, not in `workflows/`.
- README Quick Start assumes a pre-existing `venv/` and Linux `source venv/bin/activate`
  on a Windows-developed repo.

### Unverified — MUST be confirmed by the developer with real commands
1. Whether `debug_logs/` or `.env` are tracked or present in git history
   (`git ls-files`, `git log --all -- <path>`, `git log -p --all -S<secret>`).
2. The exact copyright **year** and wording in upstream's LICENSE file — must be copied
   verbatim, not paraphrased.

## Design (Product Designer, Mode C)
goal: >
  Remove the two hard release blockers for auto_grocer's first public source-only
  release: (A) eliminate real owner PII and live secrets from the working tree AND git
  history, then add an automated secret-scanner guard; and (B) establish complete,
  legally sound licensing and attribution — a root MIT LICENSE, the upstream MIT LICENSE
  reproduced inside the vendored fork, an explicit "modified from the original" NOTICE,
  a provenance note in pyproject.toml, and README disclaimer/credits copy that reframes
  the WAF/bot narrative from an evasion how-to into legitimate session maintenance. After
  Cycle 1 the repo must be safe to publish without leaking credentials or misrepresenting
  the vendored work's authorship. Cycles 2–6 are separate loops and are NOT touched here.

non_goals:
  - Package rename texas_grocery_mcp -> auto_grocer_mcp (Cycle 4).
  - Docs correctness: grocery_browser.run vs session_maintenance.run, broken README
    links, cross-platform quickstart (Cycle 2).
  - Dependency-system consolidation, duplicate DATABASE_IMPLEMENTATION.md, dead packages,
    docker-compose fallback password (Cycle 3).
  - CI / ruff coverage / type-checking / Docker build check expansion (Cycle 5).
  - CHANGELOG, v0.1.0 tag, GitHub Release (Cycle 6).
  - ANY change to on-disk runtime names: ~/.texas-grocery-mcp/ session dir, the
    auto_grocer_session Docker volume, keyring SERVICE_NAME (permanently out of scope,
    owner decision 5).

scope_and_approach: >
  Part A (secrets/PII) MUST be completed and verified before Part B, because a history
  rewrite invalidates any commits made after it and Part B commits must land on the
  already-scrubbed history.

  PART A — Secret & PII scrub

  A-1. Working-tree inventory (read-only, no rewrite). Run and record output of:
       `git ls-files debug_logs/`, `git ls-files .env`,
       `git log --all --oneline -- .env`, `git log --all --oneline -- debug_logs/`,
       and content probes `git log -p --all -S"sk-ant-"`,
       `git log -p --all -S"benbond96"`, `git log -p --all -S"7463103707"`.
       Record findings in the dev_plan. This determines whether a history rewrite is
       even required.
  A-2. Remove the PII-bearing files from the working tree and stop tracking them:
       delete the debug dumps under debug_logs/ (the four named in blocker A1 plus any
       sibling session_*/ dumps), and confirm .env is untracked. Add/confirm a
       `debug_logs/` ignore rule in `.gitignore` (currently `.env` is at L1) so future
       runs never re-stage dumps. Keep a `.gitkeep` if the directory must persist.
  A-3. Add the secret-scanner guard. Introduce a gitleaks configuration and a hook:
       either `.pre-commit-config.yaml` with the gitleaks hook, or a documented
       `gitleaks` invocation, plus a `.gitleaks.toml` allowlisting the handoff files
       under `.github/agents/handoffs/` (which legitimately contain redacted example
       identifiers). This is committable without gitleaks being installed locally.
  A-4. IF and ONLY IF A-1 shows secrets/PII in history: this is a DESTRUCTIVE rewrite.
       The developer MUST (a) stop and obtain fresh explicit user approval, (b) create a
       backup immediately beforehand via `git bundle create ../auto_grocer-backup.bundle
       --all` AND a mirror clone, THEN (c) run `git filter-repo` to purge the paths
       (`--path debug_logs/ --path .env --invert-paths`) and/or replace secret strings.
       The developer MUST NOT run filter-repo unprompted.
  A-5. Secret rotation is a manual human action outside the repo and cannot be done by
       the agent: the owner must rotate the HEB account password, the Gmail IMAP app
       password, and the CLAUDE_API_KEY (sk-ant-...) if A-1 proves any were ever
       committed. The design records this as an explicit owner action item; the Tester
       verifies only that the strings are absent from tracked content/history.

  PART B — Legal, licensing, attribution (only after Part A verified)

  B-1. Add root `LICENSE` — standard MIT text, copyright the auto_grocer owner,
       year 2026.
  B-2. Reproduce upstream's MIT license verbatim at `texas_grocery_mcp/LICENSE`. The
       developer MUST fetch the real file from
       https://github.com/mgwalkerjr95/texas-grocery-mcp (v0.1.2 tag if present) and copy
       the copyright holder ("Michael Walker") and YEAR exactly — no paraphrasing. This
       is the one permitted network dependency.
  B-3. Add a top-level `NOTICE` (or `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`) stating that
       `texas_grocery_mcp/` is derived from and "modified from the original"
       texas-grocery-mcp (link the URL, name Michael Walker, cite MIT), and summarizing
       the modifications (persisted-query override loader in
       texas_grocery_mcp/clients/graphql.py, net-new tools/substitution.py, flattened
       from upstream src/ layout).
  B-4. Add a provenance note to `pyproject.toml` (e.g. a comment or a metadata field)
       referencing the upstream project and its MIT license.
  B-5. README: add a `## Disclaimer` section — not affiliated with / endorsed by H-E-B;
       H-E-B and related marks are trademarks of their owners; for personal/educational
       use only; provided "as is" without warranty.
  B-6. README: add a `## Credits` / `## Acknowledgements` section linking
       https://github.com/mgwalkerjr95/texas-grocery-mcp and crediting Michael Walker.
  B-7. Soften the WAF/bot narrative. Reword the README WAF section (~L106) and any
       docs/ maintenance text so it reads as legitimate session-refresh / maintenance
       guidance, NOT an evasion how-to. Remove framing verbs like "evade", "bypass
       detection", "avoid getting caught", "trick", "defeat". The maintenance docs
       (CLAUDE.md, session_maintenance/README.md, the refresh skills) must remain
       factually accurate about how session refresh works — soften tone only, do not
       delete true procedural steps.

acceptance_criteria:
  1. (A1) `git ls-files debug_logs/` returns no tracked HTML/JSON debug dumps (empty, or
     only a `.gitkeep`).
  2. (A1) The four named PII files are absent from the working tree: none of
     debug_logs/session_20260609_102144/20260609_102419_265495_interrupted_test.html,
     debug_logs/session_20260715_134229/20260715_134718_440347_change_store_via_ui_Exception.html,
     debug_logs/waf_probe_20260707_214811.json,
     debug_logs/waf_probe_20260707_215004.json exist on disk.
  3. (A1) `.gitignore` contains a `debug_logs/` ignore rule (in addition to the existing
     `.env` rule).
  4. (A1) `git grep -ri "benbond96"` and `git grep -ri "7463103707"` on the current tree
     return no matches (handoff files under .github/agents/handoffs/ excluded via
     pathspec `':!.github/agents/handoffs'`).
  5. (A1) `git grep -rE "HEB188002693203319808|HEB197442000236280832"` returns no matches
     in tracked files (excluding .github/agents/handoffs/).
  6. (A2) `git ls-files .env` returns empty AND `git log --all --oneline -- .env` returns
     empty (never tracked, not in history).
  7. (A2) `git log -p --all -S"sk-ant-"` returns no output (no Claude API key ever
     committed), evidencing clean history.
  8. (A1/A2) A secret scan of history passes: `gitleaks detect --no-banner --redact`
     exits 0; if gitleaks is unavailable on the host, the documented fallback
     (`git log -p --all -S"sk-ant-"`, `-S"benbond96"`, `-S"7463103707"` all empty) passes.
  9. (A1/A2) A secret-scanner guard is committed: `.pre-commit-config.yaml` referencing
     the gitleaks hook OR a `.gitleaks.toml` config file exists at repo root.
  10. (A4) Root `LICENSE` exists and its contents contain the string `MIT License`.
  11. (A3) `texas_grocery_mcp/LICENSE` exists and its contents contain both `MIT` and
      `Michael Walker`.
  12. (A3) A `NOTICE` or `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` file exists at repo root, contains the
      phrase "modified from the original", and contains the string
      `github.com/mgwalkerjr95/texas-grocery-mcp`.
  13. (A3) `pyproject.toml` contains a provenance reference matching
      `texas-grocery-mcp` (case-insensitive).
  14. (A5) README contains a section heading matching `Disclaimer` and its body contains
      "not affiliated with H-E-B" (or "not affiliated with or endorsed by H-E-B"), a
      trademark note, a personal/educational-use statement, and a no-warranty statement.
  15. (A3/A5) README contains a Credits/Acknowledgements section whose body contains
      `github.com/mgwalkerjr95/texas-grocery-mcp`.
  16. (A5) The softened WAF narrative: `git grep -riE "evade|bypass detection|avoid
      getting caught|defeat (the )?WAF"` returns no matches in README.md and docs/ (the
      maintenance procedure text in CLAUDE.md / session_maintenance/README.md remains
      present and unchanged in substance).

risks_and_dependencies:
  - DESTRUCTIVE history rewrite (A-4): `git filter-repo` permanently rewrites all commit
    SHAs on `dev`. It requires a force-push, which breaks any existing clones/forks and
    any open PRs. The developer MUST get fresh explicit user approval AND create a
    `git bundle` + mirror-clone backup immediately beforehand, and MUST NOT run it
    unprompted. If A-1 shows history is already clean, skip the rewrite entirely.
  - Upstream LICENSE verbatim copy (B-2): the exact copyright YEAR and wording are
    UNVERIFIED and must be fetched live from
    https://github.com/mgwalkerjr95/texas-grocery-mcp — the sole permitted network
    dependency. Do not fabricate the year; paraphrasing an MIT notice is a licensing
    defect.
  - gitleaks may not be installed on this Windows host. Criterion 8 provides a
    git-native fallback so verification never blocks on the tool. Criterion 9 only
    requires the config/hook be committed, not that gitleaks run locally.
  - Secret rotation (A-5) is a manual human action outside the repository. The agents
    cannot rotate the HEB password, Gmail IMAP app password, or CLAUDE_API_KEY; the owner
    must do so if any were ever committed. Tests verify absence-from-repo only.
  - Softening WAF language (B-7) must not remove accurate maintenance steps. Over-editing
    could break the refresh-heb-login / refresh-graphql-hashes skills' factual accuracy.
    Criterion 16 checks tone-word removal while asserting the procedural docs remain.
  - No live HEB session or heb.com network access is required for any acceptance
    criterion (only the one-time upstream LICENSE fetch in B-2).

criterion_8_gitkeep_negation:
  command_v: "git check-ignore -v debug_logs/.gitkeep"
  output_v: ".gitignore:41:!debug_logs/.gitkeep\tdebug_logs/.gitkeep  (exit 0)"

    NEGATION `!debug_logs/.gitkeep`; a negation match means the file is NOT
    ignored. Confirmed definitively by the ground-truth checks below.
  command_plain: "git check-ignore debug_logs/.gitkeep"
  output_plain: "(no output, exit 1)  -> file is NOT ignored"

  output_add: "add 'debug_logs/.gitkeep'  (exit 0)  -> stageable/trackable"
  command_status: "git status --porcelain debug_logs/"

  result: PASS   # negation works; .gitkeep is trackable despite debug_logs/*

regression_pytest:
  command: "./.venv-win/Scripts/python.exe -m pytest tests/unit -q"
  summary_line: "6 failed, 338 passed, 2 skipped in 7.84s"  (exit 1)
  reproduced_natively: "powershell.exe -> same summary: 6 failed, 338 passed, 2 skipped"
  failing_tests:
    - tests/unit/test_credentials.py::TestCredentialStore::test_encrypted_file_permissions
    - tests/unit/test_secure_file.py::TestWriteSecureJson::test_creates_file_with_correct_permissions
    - tests/unit/test_secure_file.py::TestWriteSecureJson::test_fixes_insecure_permissions_on_existing_file
    - tests/unit/test_secure_file.py::TestEnsureSecurePermissions::test_fixes_insecure_permissions
    - tests/unit/test_secure_file.py::TestEnsureSecurePermissions::test_leaves_secure_permissions_unchanged
    - tests/unit/test_secure_file.py::TestEnsureSecurePermissions::test_handles_world_readable_file
  root_cause: >
    Windows filesystem cannot enforce POSIX mode 0o600 — every failure is
    `assert 438 == 384` (0o666 vs 0o600) on a Windows temp path. These tests are
    OS-specific and touch secure_file.py / credentials.py, which Cycle 1 did NOT
    modify. Pre-existing on this host; NOT a Cycle 1 regression.

regression_ruff:
  command: "./.venv-win/Scripts/python.exe -m ruff check ."
  summary_line: "Found 286 errors. [*] 204 fixable with --fix"  (exit 1)
  rule_breakdown_sample: "F821 (undefined names in a self-healing generated file), I001 (import order), W293/W291/W292, F401, F841, E722"

  config_check: >
    `pyproject.toml` [tool.ruff] extend-exclude = ["texas_grocery_mcp",
    "debug_logs", "word_dictionaries"] is INTACT; the Cycle 1 provenance comment
    sits above [project], not inside any table; `tomllib.loads` -> TOML OK.
  root_cause: >
    Pre-existing lint debt in session_maintenance/ and utility/, which are inside
    ruff scope but were never linted clean. Cycle 1 changed NO .py file, so ruff
    output is identical to baseline. NOT a Cycle 1 regression, and NOT a
    config-parse break.

regression_verdict: >
  NO REGRESSION INTRODUCED BY CYCLE 1. Proof: `git status --porcelain` shows only

### Step 4 — Adjudication of three flagged deviations

#### (A) `add_recipe_ingredients` restoration — ACCEPTED ✓

**Evidence gathered:**
1. `git diff HEAD -- mcp_server.py` shows exactly two lines added in the working tree:
   `+@mcp.tool()` and `+def add_recipe_ingredients(request: str, clear_first: bool = False) -> dict:`
   This confirms these two lines were genuinely absent at HEAD (pre-Cycle-5 state).
2. Without the decorator+def, the function body starting with the docstring through
   `return summary` was orphaned dead code after `add_products_by_id`'s
   `return _add_by_id_sync(products or [])`. Both `request` and `clear_first` in the
   body were thus undefined names (the F821 flagged at `mcp_server.py:703`).
3. The restored signature `(request: str, clear_first: bool = False) -> dict:` matches
   the orphaned docstring's Args section exactly: `request` described as a natural-language
   string and `clear_first` as an optional bool.
4. README.md and CLAUDE.md both document `add_recipe_ingredients(request)` as a primary
   tool. `mcp_server.py:9` lists it in the tool directory comment.
5. The function body references `request` at `parse_and_match(request, RecipeRepository(db))`
   and `clear_first` at `graphql_cart_sync(IL, _store_id(), do_clear=clear_first)` —
   consistent with the signature.
6. `import mcp_server` in the working tree succeeds. `hasattr(mcp_server, 'add_recipe_ingredients')` = True.
7. `add_products_by_id` still ends with `return _add_by_id_sync(products or [])` at the
   correct location; no code was accidentally moved into the wrong function.

**Verdict: ACCEPTED.** The two dropped lines were genuinely absent (confirmed by git diff),
the orphaned body was provably dead code (all F821s concentrating there), the restored
signature matches every source of truth (docstring, README, CLAUDE.md, tool directory), and
the body is internally consistent. This is a real latent bug fix that restores a documented
flagship tool. `add_products_by_id` is undisturbed.

#### (B) `session_maintenance/updated_functions` added to ruff `extend-exclude` — ACCEPTED ✓

**Evidence gathered:**
1. `head -5 session_maintenance/updated_functions/change_store_via_ui.py` shows:
   `# Auto-generated by nodriver self_healing on 2026-07-15 18:58:13`,
   `# Original function: change_store_via_ui`, `# Source file: /app/session_maintenance/flows.py`,
   `# Healing attempt: 3`, `# Error that triggered rewrite: ...`.
   The file is confirmed machine-generated output.
2. `grep -rn "from session_maintenance.updated_functions\|import session_maintenance.updated_functions"
   . --include="*.py"` → no results. The directory is never imported as a module.
   `scripts/apply_updates.py` reads the file as TEXT (via `open()`) and splices it into
   `session_maintenance/flows.py`, where all undefined names resolve in context.
3. The 20 undefined names (HEB_HOME, random_time, is_visible, click_element, etc.) are all
   defined in `session_maintenance/flows.py` in the host module — they are expected free
   names in a code fragment, not real bugs.
4. Excluding the directory does not hide F821s in hand-authored code; it is the same
   class of exclusion as `debug_logs` (precedent from Cycle 3).

**Verdict: ACCEPTED.** The file is generated, never imported as a module, and the F821s
are structural artifacts of a code fragment, not real bugs. Excluding via `extend-exclude`
(not `# noqa`) is the correct mechanism and follows the established project precedent.

#### (C) Five unanticipated ruff rules — ACCEPTED ✓

**Evidence gathered:**
1. The four auto-fixable unanticipated rules (W291, F541, E703, W292) were cleaned by
   extending the `--fix` pass; all are deterministic cosmetic fixes with no behavior impact.
2. E402(3) uses `# noqa: E402` on exactly 3 imports in `scripts/seed_from_sources.py`:
   - Line 24: `import mcp_server as M  # noqa: E402`
   - Line 25: `from recipe_grabber import extract_recipe_metadata  # noqa: E402`
   - Line 26: `from utility.youtube import is_youtube_url, parse_ingredients_from_text  # noqa: E402`
   All three appear AFTER `sys.path.insert(0, _ROOT)` at line 23. The preceding imports
   (`os`, `sys`, `requests`, `BeautifulSoup`) are standard/third-party and do NOT need the
   sys.path manipulation — correctly placed before it. The three flagged imports require the
   path modification to resolve and cannot be moved before it without breaking the script.
   The `# noqa: E402` annotation is the standard and correct way to suppress this rule for
   post-`sys.path` imports. No behavior change.
3. Total pre-fix count (286) is confirmed unchanged from baseline; post-fix count is 0. The
   auto-fix set extension (adding W291, F541, E703, W292 to the `--fix` run) introduced no
   observable behavior change — all four are whitespace/punctuation cosmetics.

**Verdict: ACCEPTED.** The four auto-fixable rules are harmless. The E402 `# noqa`
annotations are legitimate, minimal, and placed exactly at the three imports that require
a prior `sys.path` manipulation.
